title: Writing Minutes of Meeting
overview: Accurate and well-structured meeting minutes provide an essential record of discussions, decisions, responsibilities, and agreed actions. Effective minutes are not a word-for-word transcript; they are a concise, objective, and reliable business document that allows participants and stakeholders to understand what was considered, what was decided, and what must happen next.

This practical course develops the skills required to prepare for meetings, capture relevant information efficiently, distinguish essential content from unnecessary detail, and transform notes into clear and professional minutes. Participants will learn how to record decisions and action points accurately, use appropriate business language, maintain neutrality, organize information logically, and apply consistent formatting.

The program also addresses the complete minutes cycle—from preparation and note-taking to drafting, reviewing, approval, distribution, and follow-up. Through realistic meeting scenarios and writing exercises, participants will practice producing concise minutes that support accountability, continuity, and effective organizational communication.
audience: Executive secretaries, personal assistants, administrative assistants, office administrators, coordinators, committee secretaries, project support staff, and employees responsible for attending meetings, taking notes, preparing minutes, recording decisions, or following up agreed actions.
methodology: The course uses a highly practical methodology combining short presentations with sample-minute analysis, note-taking exercises, simulated meetings, listening activities, drafting practice, editing exercises, action-tracking activities, and individual and group feedback. Participants will work with realistic meeting situations and progressively convert raw notes into accurate, concise, and professionally structured minutes.
objectivesIntro: By the end of the course, participants will be able to:
objectives: Explain the purpose, value, and principal characteristics of professional meeting minutes.
Prepare effectively for different types of meetings before the meeting begins.
Apply practical listening and note-taking techniques to capture essential information.
Distinguish decisions, actions, key discussion points, and supporting detail from unnecessary conversation.
Write concise, objective, and accurate minutes using appropriate business language.
Record motions, decisions, responsibilities, deadlines, and action points clearly.
Structure and format minutes so that information can be reviewed and followed easily.
Edit and proofread draft minutes for clarity, consistency, accuracy, and completeness.
Manage approval, distribution, confidentiality, and storage of meeting records appropriately.
Use minutes and action logs as practical tools for accountability and follow-up.
